rv.q: The presence as Juliet’s mother of Marisa Berenson, who graced so many magazine covers in the Seventies, feels like a deliciously unexpected collector’s item.
This is an efficient and good-looking production that comes nowhere near your heartstrings.
The pair power through with appropriately teenage high drama, but the show never plumbs the full depths of tragedy.
But when the frocks and the fights are the high points, it is indeed a story of woe.
For me, Branagh and Ashford’s version is deliciously stylish and fashionably sophisticated.
Though it is stylish, accessible and illuminated by Lily James, it misses the passionate intensity of the tragedy.
While this production fails to do justice to the play, Timothy Sheader and Dale Rooks’ Running Wild turns a second-rate script into a joyous theatrical adventure.

cn.t: Branagh's 1950s-set Romeo and Juliet draws mixed reviews: Lily James shines as Juliet, but Madden's Romeo falls flat, and the production prioritizes style over depth.
